{
  "jobspec": "#!/usr/bin/env bash

# Flux batch script
#
# LSF -> Flux notes:
# -BSUB -J RNAseq : not translated (no portable Flux equivalent in-script).
#   Performance/ops implication: job identification may be less convenient; runtime performance unaffected.
# -BSUB -o/-e logs/snakemake_%J.{out,err} : Flux can set output via `flux batch -o output=...`,
#   but LSF %J expansion is not available portably here.
#   Performance implication: none; operational implication: logs may overwrite unless you make filenames unique.
# -BSUB -q rna : site-specific queue; no portable Flux equivalent.
#   Performance implication: job may run on any eligible resources; not forcing the rna queue.
# -BSUB -R "select[mem>4] rusage[mem=4]" : memory selection/rusage not translated.
#   Performance implication: without a memory reservation/limit, the job may be placed on nodes with insufficient free memory, risking OOM or memory contention.
#
# Resource requirements in the LSF header do not specify CPUs/hosts explicitly; therefore no Flux -N/-n/-c is requested here.
# Submit with defaults, or add site-appropriate Flux resource flags if needed, e.g.:
#   flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c <cores> -t <time> ./rnaseq.flux.sh

set -o nounset -o pipefail -o errexit -x

module load singularity/3.9.2

# LSF arguments used by Snakemake for *sub-jobs* via DRMAA.
# NOTE: Flux does not provide a DRMAA interface by default. This `--drmaa` configuration will not work under Flux
# unless your site provides a DRMAA layer that targets Flux.
# Performance implication: if omitted/unsupported, Snakemake will not offload rules as separate scheduled jobs;
# it will run tasks locally within the single allocation, reducing parallelism and throughput for multi-rule workflows.
args=' \
  -q rna \
  -o {log}.out \
  -e {log}.err \
  -J {params.job_name} \
  -R "{params.memory} span[hosts=1] " \
  -n {threads} '

snakemake \
    --drmaa "$args" \
    --snakefile Snakefile \
    --configfile config.yaml \
    --jobs 12 \
    --latency-wait 60 \
    --rerun-incomplete \
    --use-singularity \
    --singularity-args "--bind /beevol/home/rbilab --bind /beevol/home/wellskri --bind /beevol/home/wellskri/packages/bin --bind /tmp:/tmp"
"
}
